from pathlib import Path

reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')

print('\\n'.join(Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').read_text().splitlines()[:250]))

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
links=set()
for page in reader.pages:
    for a in page.get('/Annots',[]):
        obj=a.get_object()
        act=obj.get('/A',{})
        if '/URI' in act: links.add(str(act['/URI']))
print('External links:', '\\n'.join(sorted(links)))
PY"

strengths: Addresses a useful problem: personalizing predictions for unseen federated clients without labeled fine-tuning. Selecting a small expert subset per client, followed by per-sample routing, provides a coherent mechanism for sparse deployment. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b09/review-experiment-0g58daxo/call-63d738d1c8864ce2872723e84b195479/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The reported improvements are promising. Tables 1–2 show 95.7% accuracy on CIFAR10, 78.6% on CIFAR100, and 83.27% on CIFAR100 when experts receive pretrained initialization, versus 73.73% for the common model.

The equations and pseudocode make the core algorithm understandable. Ablations on common-model quality, initialization, anchor frequency, and label distributions provide useful evidence about stability, including candidly reported failure cases.
weaknesses: Baseline reliability is the main obstacle to acceptance. In Table 1, CIFAR10 FedAvg and FedMix deteriorate from a 93% pretrained model to 58.4% and 42.9%, respectively; SCAFFOLD reaches chance-level performance. Appendix B.1 acknowledges learning-rate inconsistency with pretraining, but systematic tuning and failure diagnostics are not documented. These comparisons do not convincingly distinguish algorithmic superiority from avoidable baseline optimization failures.

The demonstrated applicability is substantially narrower than the broad claims suggest. Main experiments construct anchors with distinct label groups and allocate half of client participation to them. Figures 5 and 9 show substantial deterioration without this sampling mechanism. The overlapping-label experiments are useful, but practical anchor identification and availability remain unvalidated. Evaluation covers synthetic label shifts on two CIFAR datasets, rather than broader client or feature-distribution shifts.

Efficiency and scalability are insufficiently substantiated. Table 1 compares FedJETs with 5–10 total experts against FedMix with two, while normal FedJETs clients train two ResNet34 models versus one for FedAvg. Appendix F provides useful equal-expert-count controls, but there are no measurements of transmitted bytes, computation, memory, or latency, including common-model pretraining and deployment. Communication rounds alone cannot establish the claimed resource advantages.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite the algorithm description. Exact common-model pretraining data and procedures, checkpoint selection, per-client training sample counts, gating-network dimensions, and baseline tuning configurations are missing. No code link or repeated-run uncertainty is provided. These omissions matter particularly because performance changes sharply with common-model quality and client sampling.

Originality is not sufficiently isolated or positioned. The contribution combines established mixture routing, pretrained representations, and fixed anchor assignments, but the relationship to mixture-distribution federated learning such as FedEM is underdeveloped. Appendix H's K-means visualization does not establish that clustered alternatives cannot work. Controls holding anchors and capacity fixed while varying routing would clarify the gating mechanism's added value.

Several reporting claims exceed their evidence. The assertion of near-perfect expert selection is difficult to reconcile with Table 4's 27.1% CIFAR100 error, whose routing-correctness criterion is not clearly defined. Some appendix tables select the best test accuracy across training without explaining validation-based checkpoint selection. These issues weaken confidence in the interpretation of the results.

The claim of operating 'without violating data privacy' needs qualification. Keeping raw data local does not establish privacy for transmitted model updates or expert selections, and no threat model or privacy analysis is supplied. This is an unsupported guarantee, rather than evidence of a separate serious ethical violation.
